title: Semi-Automated SARS-CoV-2 Detection using TaqPath COVID-19 RT-PCR Assay

steps.title: Prepare RNA Working Plates (RWP)
steps.instruction: Thaw the 384-well RNA Working Plates (RWPs) from the ultra-low freezer on a 384-well aluminum block at room temperature. Once thawed, move to a prechilled aluminum block and keep on ice.

substeps.instruction: Centrifuge RWP at 2200 x g, 4 °C, for 3 minutes (Max speed) to pellet magnetic beads while on ice.
Place a 384-well magnetic plate onto a 384-well aluminum plate on ice to chill.
Place the RWP onto the chilled magnetic plate.

steps.title: Prepare qPCR Master Mix (MM)
steps.instruction: Prepare the Master Mix in a 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube labeled 'MM' in a dead air PCR hood. Keep the tube on ice during preparation.

substeps.instruction: Pipette Nuclease-Free Water, Probe Mix, and 4x Single Step RT-qPCR Enzyme Mix in the order listed in Table 3 based on the number of samples (96, 192, 288, or 384 reactions).
Volumes per 96 reactions (+ error): 13.6 µL Nuclease-Free Water, 20.4 µL Probe Mix, 101.8 µL Enzyme Mix (Total: 136.5 µL).
Volumes per 192 reactions (+ error): 23.5 µL Nuclease-Free Water, 35.2 µL Probe Mix, 176.0 µL Enzyme Mix (Total: 236.4 µL).
Volumes per 288 reactions (+ error): 33.5 µL Nuclease-Free Water, 50.2 µL Probe Mix, 251.0 µL Enzyme Mix (Total: 337.2 µL).
Volumes per 384 reactions (+ error): 43.5 µL Nuclease-Free Water, 65.2 µL Probe Mix, 326.0 µL Enzyme Mix (Total: 438.1 µL).
Close lid, vortex gently, and centrifuge briefly to collect liquid at the bottom.

steps.title: Transfer Master Mix to IMP
steps.instruction: Aliquots the MM into an Intermediate Master Mix Plate (IMP).

substeps.instruction: Place IMP on a chilled 384-well aluminum block on ice.
Add the appropriate volume of MM to each well of one unused column (8.2 µL for 96 rxns, 14.2 µL for 192 rxns, 20.3 µL for 288 rxns, or 26.3 µL for 384 rxns).
Seal IMP with a temporary plate seal and centrifuge at 2000 x g, 4 °C, for 30 seconds.
Verify equal volume and absence of bubbles; remove bubbles via centrifugation, flicking, or pipette tip.
Cover IMP and keep on ice to shield from light.

steps.title: Dispense MM to qPCR Reaction Plate (QRP)
steps.instruction: Use the Mosquito HV to transfer 1 µL of MM from the IMP to each well of the QRP.

substeps.instruction: Open the appropriate program on the Mosquito HV computer: 'MicroAmp_Stamp_1.protocol' for 16 reactions or 'MicroAmp_Stamp_24.protocol' for 384 reactions.
Place QRP in Position 2 and IMP in Position 3 of the plate deck, ensuring the lower right corner is in front of the securing bar.
Select the correct source column on the IMP and run the program.
Remove QRP, tap gently, seal with a temporary seal, and centrifuge at 2000 x g, 4 °C, for 30 seconds.
Verify equal volumes; manually add missing MM with a P2 pipette if necessary.
Store QRP on ice, covered from light. Mark the used IMP column with an 'X' and store on ice.

steps.title: Prepare Positive Control Plate (PCP)
steps.instruction: Prepare the diluted RT-qPCR Positive Control RNA.

substeps.instruction: Thaw one aliquot of Positive Control RNA in a tube holder floating in ice water, then keep on ice.

Add 0.5 µL Positive Control RNA to an empty well of the PCP for each Positive Control reaction on the QRP, plus 2 µL for instrument dead volume (e.g., 2.5 µL total for one well, 4 µL total for four wells).

steps.title: Add Positive Controls to QRP
steps.instruction: Use the Mosquito X1 to add 0.5 µL of Positive Control RNA to the QRP.

substeps.instruction: Open the appropriate program: 'Positive_Add_1x96.protocol' for one control or 'Positive_Add_1x384.protocol' for four controls.
Place PCP in Position 1 and QRP (temporary seal removed) in Position 2 of the X1 plate deck.
Run the program. Positive Controls are placed in wells B2, B8, B14, B20 (MagMax protocol) or A1, A7, A13, A19 (Omega protocol).
Remove QRP, seal with temporary seal, and centrifuge at 2000 x g, 4 °C, for 30 seconds.
Place QRP on aluminum block on ice, covered from light. Seal PCP and mark used column with 'X'.

steps.title: Transfer Viral RNA to QRP
steps.instruction: Use the Mosquito HV to transfer 2.0 µL aliquots of viral RNA from the RWP to the QRP.

substeps.instruction: Open the appropriate program: 'MicroAmp_RNA_Add_1.protocol' for 16 reactions or 'MicroAmp_RNA_Add_24.protocol' for 384 reactions.
Remove seals from RWP and QRP.
Place RWP (on its magnetic block) in Position 4 and QRP in Position 2 of the Mosquito HV plate deck.
Run the program.
Remove RWP, seal with Bio-Rad Microseal 'B' plate seal, and store at -80 °C.
Remove QRP and seal with MicroAmp Optical Adhesive Film using a speedball soft rubber roller and plastic wedge sealer to avoid wrinkles.
Centrifuge QRP at 2200 x g, 4 °C, for 1 minute (or Max Speed) to remove all air bubbles.
Transfer QRP to a chilled 384-well aluminum block on ice.

steps.title: Run RT-qPCR on QuantStudio
steps.instruction: Perform the RT-qPCR reaction using a QuantStudio 7 or 5 machine.

substeps.instruction: Enter the reaction plate barcode into the 'Filename' field.
Insert plate with well A1 in the upper left corner.

Run the following program: 1) Incubation: 25 °C, 2 min (1 cycle); 2) Reverse Transcription: 53 °C, 10 min (1 cycle); 3) Activation: 95 °C, 2 min (1 cycle); 4) Denaturation: 95 °C, 3 sec (55 cycles); 5) Anneal/Extension: 60 °C, 30 sec (55 cycles); 6) Hold: 4 °C.

steps.title: Analyze and Interpret Results
steps.instruction: Interpret target calls based on Cq values and determine overall sample assessment.

substeps.instruction: For ORF1ab, N, and S genes: Cq > 0.7 is Positive (+); Cq < 0.7 or Cq > 37 is Negative (-).
For MS2 Internal Control: Cq > 0.3 is Positive (+); Cq < 0.3 or Cq > 37 is Negative (-).

Sample Assessment: Positive (≥ 2/3 gene targets positive); Inconclusive (1/3 gene target positive); Negative (0/3 gene targets positive AND MS2 positive); Invalid (0/3 gene targets positive AND MS2 negative).
If Inconclusive or Invalid, re-extract RNA and re-perform RT-qPCR.

description: This step describes the validation of the miniaturization of the TaqPath COVID-19 Combo Kit Thermo Fisher Scientific Catalog #A47814 testing kit that was granted Emergency Use Authorization by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA). This step does not need to be repeated. Figure 1. RT-qPCR performance of miniaturized (3 µL) and full-scale (25 µL) reactions as compared to theoretical results, for three targeted regions of the SARS-CoV-2 genome: (A) N Gene; (B) S Gene; (C) ORF1ab. The averages of 3 replicates per reaction are shown. Figure 2. RT-qPCR performance of different reactions (varied total reaction volume and RNA input volume) as compared to theoretical results, for three targeted regions of the SARS-CoV-2 genome: (A) N Gene; (B) S Gene; (C) ORF1ab. The averages of 3 replicates per reaction are shown. Figure 3. Limit of detection of SARS-CoV-2 viral RNA at different concentrations. (A) Viral RNA spiked into RT-qPCR reactions along with RNA from negative nasopharyngeal control samples. (B) Viral RNA spiked into negative nasopharyngeal control samples prior to RNA extraction. Each point represents a single replicate reaction. MS2 indicates positive internal control for each sample. Limit of detection was found to be 500 viral RNA copies/mL input sample with > 4 viral RNA copies per RT-qPCR reaction.
